Daily Quiz.question: ১) Which one is the oldest English Literary period?
Daily Quiz.exp: The oldest English Literary period is The Anglo-Saxon period. It was started at 450 A.D and lasted till 1066 A.D. It is also the longest English literary period in the context of duration. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Which time frame is known as Elizabethan Period?
Daily Quiz.exp: Elizabethan Period started when the Queen Elizabeth crowned which was at 1558 and continued till her death at 1603. Elizabeth I, bynames the Virgin Queen and Good Queen Bess, (born September 7, 1533, Greenwich, near London, England—died March 24, 1603, Richmond, Surrey), queen of England (1558–1603) during a period, often called the Elizabethan Age. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Elizabeth-I

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) Which time frame is known as the “Age of Chaucer”?
Daily Quiz.exp: The period between 1343 and 1450 is known as the Age of Chaucer. It marked the first significant literary age in English literature. Source: https://englishsummary.com/chaucer-age-characteristics/

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Who is the first poet of English Literature?
Daily Quiz.exp: First English poet is Caedmon. Source: https://www.britannica.com/search?query=First+English+Poet

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Which one is not a literary work of English Old Age?
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) The Legend of Good Women
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Dream of the Rood
Daily Quiz.exp: The Legend of Good Women is written by Geffery Chaucer. And the rest of the literary work from English Old Age. Source: https://www.britannica.com/art/Anglo-Saxon-literature

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) Which one is the earliest English long poem/epic?
Daily Quiz.exp: Beowulf, heroic poem, the highest achievement of Old English literature and the earliest European vernacular epic. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Beowulf

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Who supervised the compilation of the earliest English Prose “The Anglo-Saxon Chronicles”?
Daily Quiz.exp: Old English prose works include legal writings, medical tracts, religious texts, and translations from Latin and other languages. Particularly notable is the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, a historical record begun about the time of King Alfred’s reign (871–899) and continuing for more than three centuries. Source: https://www.britannica.com/art/Anglo-Saxon-literature

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Find the odd-one out-
Daily Quiz.exp: Francis Bacon was born in 1561, who was a Elizabethan Literary person. The Others are from the Middle English Period. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) Who wrote “Opus Majus”?
Daily Quiz.exp: Opus Majus, Opus Tertium-- written by Roger Bacon. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Opus-majus

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Who is the father of Modern English Poetry?
Daily Quiz.exp: Caedmon is the first English Poet, Henry Fielding is the father of English Modern Novel and Geoffrey Chaucer is the fathe of Modern English Poetry. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Who Translated the Bible/New Testament into English prose?
Daily Quiz.exp: John Wycliffe, Wycliffe also spelled Wycliff, Wyclif, Wicliffe, or Wiclif, (born c. 1330, Yorkshire, England—died December 31, 1384, Lutterworth, Leicestershire), English theologian, philosopher, church reformer, and promoter of the first complete translation of the Bible into English. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/John-Wycliffe

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Which one is the golden age of English Literature?
Daily Quiz.exp: The Elizabethan Period is called the golden English Literary period. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) Which one is not the literary work of Geoffrey Chaucer?
Daily Quiz.exp: Troilus and Cressida is a play by William Shakespear. The rests are written by Geoffrey Chaucer.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Who is considered to be the greatest dramatist of all time?
Daily Quiz.exp: William Shakespeare, Shakespeare also spelled Shakspere, byname Bard of Avon or Swan of Avon, (baptized April 26, 1564, Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England—died April 23, 1616, Stratford-upon-Avon), English poet, dramatist, and actor often called the English national poet and considered by many to be the greatest dramatist of all time. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Who was the greatest dramatist before Shakespeare?
Daily Quiz.exp: Cristopher Marlowe was the greatest dramatist before Shakespeare. Christopher Marlowe, (baptized Feb. 26, 1564, Canterbury, Kent, Eng.—died May 30, 1593, Deptford, near London), Elizabethan poet and Shakespeare’s most important predecessor in English drama, who is noted especially for his establishment of dramatic blank verse. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Christopher-Marlowe

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) Which one is not a comedy of Shakespeare?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Taming of the Shrew
Daily Quiz.exp: The Taming of the Shrew and the Merchant of Venice are comedy; The Two Noble Kinsmen is a tragicomedy and Timon of Athens is a tragedy. Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) Who is not a university wit?
Daily Quiz.exp: Among these, Thomas Sackville was not a university wit. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/University-Wits

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Which one is first tragedy in English literature?
Daily Quiz.exp: Gorboduc, play by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville that takes as its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain. First performed in 1561, it is the earliest English tragic play in blank verse. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Gorboduc-by-Norton-and-Sackville

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Who established dramatic ‘blank verse’?
Daily Quiz.exp: Christopher Marlowe, (baptized Feb. 26, 1564, Canterbury, Kent, Eng.—died May 30, 1593, Deptford, near London), Elizabethan poet and Shakespeare’s most important predecessor in English drama, who is noted especially for his establishment of dramatic blank verse. Source:https://www.britannica.com/biography/Christopher-Marlowe
